note: The bands the E-flite Night Timber X 1.2m plant has to land in, from docs/NIGHTTIMBER-STAGE1.md, which derives each from E-flite's manual and product pages, its photographs, APC's data for the 13 x 4E prop and momentum theory (scripts/nighttimber-derive.js prints the derived figures). E-flite publishes no bench or flight figure, so the performance bands are about derived figures built on an ESTIMATED motor and drag, and each says how wide and why; the widths are the Extra's (tests/extra-thresholds.json) for the same reasons. Never widened to pass; argue in the derivation instead.

n1_level_75.source: level speed at 75 percent throttle, derived 12.34 from the estimated thrust line and drag polar; 12 percent either way. Derived 17.43 since then, re-derived 2026-10-11 on APC's 13 x 4E curve (prop curves, npm run prop:curves -- wings), was 12.34 on the straight line; the same 12 percent about it.

n2_stall.source: flaps up: sqrt(2W / rho S CLmax), derived 9.08 at 1698 g on the clean 0.287 m^2 and the Turbo Timber's CLmax of 1.15; alphaStall is CLmax / CLalpha, 1.15 / 4.904. 0.94 to 1.14 of the formula, the Kadet's and the Extra's proportion, since the plant reads the stall at the blend's midpoint Re-derived 2026-10-11: alphaStall over the wing's own slope, a_w 4.494 (scripts/nighttimber-derive.js), not the wing and tail's 4.9038: the stall angle is the wing's and the tail's share lifts on past it, as the Extra's (#935); was 0.23451. And the band with it: the plant's CLmax is the wing's 1.150 plus the tail's lift at that angle, on its own angle, (CLa - a_w) (sin a - de/da a - a_0 (1 - de/da)) / (1 - de/da) = 0.091, so the formula's speeds go by sqrt(1.150 / 1.241) = 0.9626.

n2b_stall_flaps.source: full flaps, power off, the nose raised slowly (wingpilot.js stallSpeed, from 11 m/s as the Timber's T4): the real aircraft's own figure, the video's pilot's 15 to 18 mph, 6.7 to 8.0 m/s, with full flaps (analysis/3D-VIDEO-LESSONS.md 19:20). The derivation's sqrt(2W / rho S CLmax) with the plain flap's Raymer increment is 8.08, at the band's top: it leaves out the flap mix's down elevator and the tail's share, which the plant flies; since #854 (CL max at the top of the curve) the plant reads 7.3 at the linear crossing, alphaStall (CLmax + clmax_df df - dCL(df)) / CLalpha. Re-derived to the real aircraft on 2026-10-09 after #854, docs/NIGHTTIMBER-STAGE1.md Re-derived 2026-10-11: alphaStall over the wing's own slope, a_w 4.494 (scripts/nighttimber-derive.js), not the wing and tail's 4.9038: the stall angle is the wing's and the tail's share lifts on past it, as the Extra's (#935); was 0.2035.

n3_glide.source: L/D at 11 m/s, derived 8.18, 12 percent either way

n4_top.source: level speed at full throttle, derived 17.10, 10 percent either way: a 13 x 4's pitch speed is 19.2 m/s. Derived 23.58 since then, re-derived 2026-10-11 on APC's 13 x 4E curve (prop curves, npm run prop:curves -- wings), was 17.10 on the straight line; the same 10 percent about it. The pitch speed no longer caps it: APC's 13 x 4E thrust holds on past the geometric pitch, 19.2 m/s, and runs out at about 1.45 times it, so the top speed is mu 1.23 on the curve where the line stopped it at 0.89.

n5_roll.source: pb/2V at full aileron on the high rate, the flaps mixed in as full span ailerons, Clda throw_a / -Clp, derived 0.301 (373 deg/s at 13 m/s); 25 percent either way, the width the large deflection correction K' carries

n6_hover.source: hanging on the prop, the nose held up by the elevator and rudder in the slipstream, the height on the throttle: sqrt(W / T_static), derived 0.8015; 5 percent either way. The video's pilot hovers at about 55 to 65 percent by eye (07:38), a thumb on a radio whose throttle curve is not known; the plant's thrust goes as the stick squared, so this is the estimate's figure, not the video's Since 2026-10-11 the prop turns at sqrt(W / T_static), 0.8015 of full, at a duty of 0.7776 on the electric motor's own law, n^2 + 5.667 n = 6.667 d (plant_wing.c prop_spool, docs/FLIGHTMODEL.md "The electric throttle"); the same 5 percent about it.

n7_vertical.source: straight up at full throttle, where the thrust meets the weight and the zero lift drag, derived 6.60; 10 percent either way. Derived 11.12 since then, re-derived 2026-10-11 on APC's 13 x 4E curve (prop curves, npm run prop:curves -- wings), was 6.60 on the straight line; the same 10 percent about it.

n8_torque_roll.source: hanging at the hover throttle with the ailerons let go: the prop's 0.243 N m of reaction less the swirl's root and fin shares (SWIRL_KEEP 0.74, Selig AIAA 2010-7938), 0.161 N m, against the air the turning airframe sweeps through (rot_k roll), derived 216 deg/s to the left; 25 percent either way. The video's pilot holds a slower 75 deg/s with the ailerons (15:06)

n9_aileron_hover.source: the same with full right aileron: the full span ailerons' inboard share in the slipstream, dp fa S b Clda throw_a, 0.239 N m, against the net torque, derived 151 deg/s right; 40 percent either way, the difference of two estimates. Without the flaps mixed in the ailerons start outside the slipstream and this is nothing

n10_zero_speed.source: hanging still, full up elevator and full right rudder from rest: the wash's dp on the surfaces' immersed shares, saturating on a flat plate at the control's angle, derived 40.78 in pitch and 22.33 in yaw; 25 percent either way. With the prop stopped, under 5 percent of it

n13_rest.source: E-flite's side photograph: the spinner's axis 4.5 deg nose up of the ground, the CG 0.2562 m up, 21.5 percent of the weight on the tailwheel; half a degree, 5 mm and 3.5 points either way

n14_takeoff.source: full throttle from standing with half flaps, the tail up at 5 m/s and the nose to 8 deg: liftoff at 8.5 m/s after 3.91 m (nighttimber:derive); 40 percent short and 60 long, the Extra's, since the plant's roll has the gear's springs and the pilot's hands in it and the derivation has neither. Derived 3.09 m (3.085), re-derived 2026-10-11 on APC's 13 x 4E curve (prop curves, npm run prop:curves -- wings), was 3.91 on the straight line; the same 40 percent short and 60 long about it.

n15_unmoved.source: every other aircraft's recorded flight hash in Node, as main's module (ad6db961) flies them without the Night Timber: it adds a table, its parts and its own id, 30, and moves nothing else

n16_cross_host.source: the Night Timber's recorded take off, hover, torque roll and flight, state trace hash, Node against headless Chrome

n17_person_hover.source: can a person hover it, as the real one is hovered (analysis/3D-VIDEO-LESSONS.md, 07:38 and 15:00)? scripts/hover-probe.js's person paced pilot (0.2 s late, ten moves a second in fiftieths of the stick, McRuer and Jex), its 648 pilot grid, flying the video's technique: the ailerons hold a slow 75 deg/s torque roll rather than stopping it (study.mjs hoverLaw 'video'), in AS3X, the receiver as the aircraft ships. At least one pilot of the grid holds the nose within 20 deg of vertical and the height within 10 m for 10 s. The count is reported for Manual and AS3X, both techniques
